priority.note: final rank = min(last index, base_index + trend_bonus + citizen_bonus); wording is always 'Recommend ...' because the system does not itself deploy/notify

rules.action: Recommend routine monitoring; no urgent intervention required
rules.explanation: Risk level is LOW - standard watchkeeping suffices

rules.action: Recommend increased monitoring frequency of rainfall and local water levels
rules.explanation: Moderate risk warrants closer observation than routine

rules.description: Moderate risk but rising: prepare resources
rules.action: Recommend preparing response resources for possible escalation
rules.explanation: Rising trend at MODERATE level justifies advance preparation

rules.action: Recommend inspection of drainage choke points and low-lying stretches
rules.explanation: High risk raises probability of drainage-related waterlogging

rules.action: Recommend deployment readiness / pre-positioning of response resources
rules.explanation: High risk justifies having resources ready nearby

rules.action: Recommend issuing an appropriate public advisory through official channels
rules.explanation: High risk merits proactive public communication

rules.action: Recommend targeted monitoring of known vulnerable low-lying zones
rules.explanation: High risk concentrates impact in structurally vulnerable areas

rules.action: Recommend immediate activation of response procedures
rules.explanation: Critical risk leaves no margin for delayed reaction

rules.action: Recommend deployment of emergency resources at priority locations
rules.explanation: Critical risk calls for resources at the most exposed spots first

rules.action: Recommend notifying disaster-management personnel through established channels
rules.explanation: Critical risk requires institutional awareness beyond this system

rules.action: Recommend issuing an urgent public advisory
rules.explanation: Critical risk justifies urgent public-facing communication

rules.action: Recommend continuous monitoring until conditions ease below CRITICAL
rules.explanation: Critical states must be tracked without interruption

rules.description: Rising trend escalates preparedness at HIGH/CRITICAL
rules.action: Recommend escalating preparedness measures given the rising risk trend
rules.explanation: A rising trend at already-elevated levels argues for stronger action than a stable one

rules.description: Falling trend allows step-down of special measures
rules.action: Recommend maintaining only the standard monitoring cycle as conditions improve
rules.explanation: Improving trend with non-critical level reduces need for extraordinary measures

rules.description: Any citizen reports: field verification as evidence
rules.action: Recommend field verification of the citizen-reported incident(s) and inclusion as contextual evidence
rules.explanation: Citizen reports are contextual signals that deserve on-ground confirmation, not automatic truth

rules.action: Recommend treating the clustered citizen reports as priority evidence for inspection resourcing
rules.explanation: Multiple independent reports in one zone indicate a probable real incident pattern
